items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: I used to go over there by this fellow there, what you call him, the guitar player, what his name is? ... Eddie Connors, yeah. He's a little bit around the corner from him.

ctx.x: When did they start all the solo business down here?

Oh, well, when they started, first I heard it was in New York in 45. I went up at Bunk Johnson. I used to go over there by this fellow there, what you call him, the guitar player, what his name is? The one who has a nightclub up there? Yeah, right around the corner from us. What his name was? Eddie? Eddie Connors, yeah. He's a little bit around the corner from him. And that's where I heard the Wild Bill Davidson, because there was scooching every fellow, you understand? Solo. But the whole time we was up there,…

You know, when I used to go up to Tyler's Big Auden in 1945, you weren't even here then, but you were in New York, I guess. I had Joe Avery and, and we were coming up there. I never heard a solo the whole time I was there. Not one solo. The trumpet would take down and that was all.
